subject: Post-demo follow-up: PII visibility, retention, and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morris <lena@careflow.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: PII visibility, retention, and next steps

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the specific answers/next steps you asked for during the demo so your security and engineering teams can review: 

1) What we store by default
- Prompts (request payloads): processed in-memory during inference. For hosted API, we keep non-identifiable telemetry and aggregated metrics by default. Prompt payloads are not persisted unless the customer enables recording.
- Outputs (model responses): not persisted by default in hosted; ephemeral caching for active sessions only.

2) Retention options and TTLs
- Hosted (default): ephemeral TTL of 24 hours for transient session caches; no long-term storage unless you opt in.
- Dedicated: configurable — customers can request retention windows from 0 (ephemeral) up to 90 days; we provide explicit controls in the Console and API.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: customer-managed; Redwood does not retain copies unless configured in your deployment.

3) Logging / audit control
- Request-level metadata (timestamps, request size, model version) stored for 90 days by default for operational observability.
- Full request/response logging is an opt-in feature (required for debugging/quality) and can be scoped per-route.

4) Data residency and encryption
- Regions: US, EU available for hosted. Dedicated clusters can be provisioned in specific AZs/regions.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS + at-rest AES-256. KMS integration available for Dedicated and Private deployments.

5) PII handling & redaction guidance
- We recommend client-side redaction for direct identifiers. For downstream processing we offer automatic token-level redaction tooling as an optional pre-processing step.

Action items I promised:
- Attach the one-pager summarizing the above (attached).
- Karthik will provide a short write-up confirming default telemetry retention windows and escalation path for audit requests.
- Marcus will add a concise line for the SOC2 / security controls we referenced.

Next step: would you like Karthik + Marcus to join a 30-minute call with your security team next week (we’re proposing Tue/Wed mornings PST)? If yes, we’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our security team so we can triage internally before scheduling a call: 

- When you say "processed in-memory" for prompts, can you confirm whether any request payloads are ever written to disk on the host (swap/temp files, dump logs) in hosted mode?
- For the 24-hour ephemeral TTL: is that a hard deletion (crypto-delete) or just removed from fast caches and still accessible in backups/archives?
- Can you share the exact API param or Console toggle name to opt in to full request/response logging? We need to map it to our internal checklist.
- For EU residency: do you have EU-hosted endpoints with separate physical clusters, and is data replicated out-of-region for HA?

Also, our compliance officer asked for a short statement we can include in the RFP that says whether Redwood ever uses customer prompt/outputs for model training or product improvement.

Hi Lena / CareFlow security —

Thanks for the questions. Below are short, customer-facing answers you can include in your RFP or share with compliance: 

1) Disk writes / ephemeral processing
- Hosted mode: request payloads are handled in-memory on inference workers. We do not write request/response bodies to local disks as part of normal processing. Temporary OS-level swap is disabled for inference hosts; we also run periodic integrity checks to ensure no core dumps are present.

2) 24-hour TTL behavior
- Ephemeral caches: items are removed from active caches and are not persisted in backups; data is eligible for zero-recovery deletion within 24 hours. For Dedicated, retention is configurable and subject to the selected storage SLA.

3) Console/API toggle names
- Console: Project Settings -> Data Capture -> "Request/Response Logging" (toggle).
- API: Pass header X-Redwood-Capture: true when creating a route to enable logs for that route.

4) EU residency and replication
- We operate separate physical clusters for the EU region (eu-1). By default we do not replicate EU-region customer data to US clusters; cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration for HA.

5) Use for training/product improvement
- Redwood does NOT use customer prompt or output payloads for model training or improving models unless explicitly opted in by the customer. Customers can elect to share anonymized telemetry for product-quality improvements via an explicit setting in the Console.

6) SOC2 / controls statement (short)
- Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II controls for our hosted control plane and publishes the report under NDA. We offer KMS integration and detailed audit logs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

7) Recommended quick mitigations for PII-sensitive flows
- Apply client-side redaction for direct identifiers, enable route-level logging only when necessary, and pin models/versions in production to avoid unexpected behavior.

Next steps:
- We can join a 30-minute call next Tue 8 Jun at 10:00 AM PST (we'll send a calendar invite if that works).
- I attached the one-pager and a short checklist for your procurement team.
